Definition: from G3060; to reproach, i.e. vilify:--revile.
BiblicalUsage: loidoréō means revile — and its range, from the ordinary to the holy, is the point. In 1 Peter 2:23, "reviled not again"; and in 1 Corinthians 4:12, "working with our own hands: being reviled". In John 9:28, "Then they reviled him"; and in Acts 23:4, "Revilest thou God's high priest?".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe reviling answered with blessing is the Christian's mark — Paul was reviled and blessed, and Christ when He was reviled reviled not again. I hold that the high priest's name is not mine to curse, and the blind man's healing is not theirs to mock. My position is that I will commit myself to Him that judgeth righteously, and leave the reviling unanswered.
